title: Safety Net Runway: Service Degradation Sandbox & Cross-Team Ops Journal
content:
Overview:
- Working journal / sandbox plan for deliberate degradation experiments and the safety-net (fallbacks, canaries, ops play) across model-serving, routing, and edge cache layers.
- Purpose: create repeatable experiments to validate SLO guardrails, owner responsibilities, and communication patterns when degradation surfaces.
- Intended audience: SREs, platform eng, serving-runtime, product-hosted-api, solutions-eng.

Goals:
1) Validate that automated fallback and routing policies keep critical paths above "minimum safe SLO" (p95 latency <= 350ms for interactive routes, error rate < 0.5% for core text-gen).
2) Harden incident runbooks so triage-to-remediation time < 30m for common degradations (cache eviction storms, model OOM, KV cache hot-shard).
3) Establish a lightweight owner matrix and escalation ladder for cross-team outages.
4) Produce metrics and artifacts to feed into the SLO review and operational budget decisions next quarter.

Scope (what we'll intentionally touch):
- Model-serving layer: variant fallbacks, model-variant throttles, quantized vs full precision variants.
- Routing layer: smart-routing policy toggles (low-cost vs low-latency pools), regional shift simulation.
- Cache/batching: forced cache misses, prefix cache TTL adjustments, batch size reduction experiments.
- Observability: add synthetic traffic for heavy tail latencies, per-route token breakdown, and error taxonomy tagging.
- Excluded: infra-level noisy neighbor mitigation (handled separately by infra team).

Hypotheses to test (short):
- H1: Enabling prefix-KV cache with TTL hysteresis reduces p95 by ~20% under bursty traffic while keeping errors steady.
- H2: Automatic fallback to smaller context/quantized models increases error rate for edge cases but keeps availability within SLO.
- H3: Routing policy that prioritizes latency over cost during detected degradation reduces user-facing errors at <2x cost increase.

Experiment matrix (quick matrix rows):
- Experiment A: Cache TTL drop by 50% + synthetic burst (owner: Priya) 
  - Inputs: 10k qps synthetic, route=chat-interactive, seq_len distribution +-20%
  - Observables: p50/p95/p99 latency, 5xx types, cache hit ratio
- Experiment B: Model fallback to quantized-mini for 10% of traffic (owner: João)
  - Inputs: 1% traffic slow ramp -> 10% sustained for 15m
  - Observables: semantic regression sample, error delta, latency delta
- Experiment C: Smart-routing regional shift (owner: Leah)
  - Inputs: simulate region outage, flip routing to adjacent region with warm pool
  - Observables: tail latency, cross-region egress, user-perceived failures

Owner matrix (actionable):
- Incident identification & initial triage: eng-sre oncall (primary), serving-runtime lead (secondary)
- Fallback policy toggles / immediate mitigations: serving-runtime (primary), platform-engineering (secondary)
- Cache/batching tuning and kernel adjustments: applied-ml (primary), infra (secondary)
- Communication + customer notices: product-hosted-api + solutions-eng

Safety & gating rules (must pass before wider rollout):
- Canary window: 30m with non-zero user traffic replica (min 500 requests).
- Regression check: sample of 200 inline semantic eval prompts, automated diff with human spot-check for anomalies > 3% quality drop.
- Metrics safety: no >1% increase in critical 5xx categories, p95 not exceed target by >2x for canary window.

Runbook snippets (quick actionable snippets for common scenarios):
- Cache storm (eviction surge):
  1) Identify cache hit ratio drop via obs dashboard (tag: cache-hit-gns).
  2) If p95 > threshold, enable TTL hysteresis policy rollback and increase cache size on warm pool (owner: applied-ml).
  3) If still failing after 10m, trigger fallback to model-variant with lower KV dependence (serving-runtime).
- Model OOM during load:
  1) Scale down request concurrency per-host via routing throttle (platform-engineering).
  2) Shift canary traffic away from impacted hosts, drain and reprovision.
  3) If repeated, revert to previous model version with lower memory footprint and open a follow-up ticket with applied-ml for quantization audit.

Observability checklist (what to create/adjust before experiments):
- Synthetic traffic generators per route (script repo link in linked_artifacts).
- Add semantic regression harness with automated sampling and store outputs for postmortem.
- Per-route token cost and latency breakdown (tokenize at ingress and measure at exit).
- Add a short-lived dashboard for the sandbox experiments with p50/p95/p99, 5xx by type, cache-hit ratio, fallback-rate, and cross-region egress.

Comms plan (internal + customer):
- Internal: #sre-ops channel pinned updates every 10m during experiments; full async postmortem in Confluence within 48h.
- External (if user-impacting): product-hosted-api to draft incident notice template, legal to review if SLAs triggered.

Timing & milestones (sprint-aligned):
- Week 0 (prep): infra for synthetic traffic + dashboards + owners assigned. (2w)
- Week 2: small canaries (10% traffic windows) for Experiment A & B.
- Week 4: cross-region shift dry-run (Experiment C) during low-traffic window.
- Week 6: failure injection day, full spidering (controlled) + final recommendation doc for SLO steering committee.

Acceptance criteria for successful experiment set:
- Defined remediation path reduced mean time to mitigation by >= 25% vs baseline.
- Semantic quality regression < 3% for sampled prompts when fallback active.
- No persistent SLO breach for primary customer-critical routes during the test suite.

Open questions / risks to capture quickly:
- How do we measure "semantic quality" in a cost-efficient automated way? (Leah prototyping a cheap embed-based delta + small human panel.)
- Legal/regulatory: cross-region shifting may be restricted for some enterprise customers. Need allowlist.
- Cost: worst-case routing policy increases egress; we need budget guardrails.

Artifacts to produce after run:
- Short postmortem template with timeline, root cause, mitigation, follow-ups, signal screenshots.
- Owner action list with due dates (Jira tickets created from this doc).
- SLO steering recommendation: keep/adjust SLO, adopt new guardrail, or change SLA tiers.

Next steps (this week):
- Priya: stand up synthetic traffic generator and confirm synthetic distribution matches prod p95 tail. Due: 2026-02-22.
- João: prepare model-variant toggle in serving-runtime feature-flag with rollback hook. Due: 2026-02-24.
- Leah: draft semantic evaluation harness and initial sampling plan. Due: 2026-02-26.
- Marcus (owner): schedule cross-team dry-run and preflight checklist review. Due: 2026-02-27.

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider a lightweight "degradation-score" that weights latency, error-type, and semantic drift to drive routing decisions automatically.
- Keep small manual playground for product folks to run a 5-min degrade test to validate UX surface.
- Archive experiment data into Incidents bucket for future SLO-economics modeling.

Bottom line: this doc is a living journal. We will iterate on small, safe experiments that exercise fallbacks and routing so the larger SLO program can adopt operational practices that are battle-tested across teams.

-- end of journal entry
